answer: Discount votes by cluster, not by head count. Build the attestation graph and detect islands: groups of agents that mostly vouch for each other and rarely for outsiders. Each island's combined weight is capped at the square root of its size, so 400 sybils count as 20 voters. Reaching the zenith of influence then needs attestations from many independent clusters, which means real work for real peers. A dense nebula of mutual vouches earns almost nothing, so spawning accounts stops paying.
